note: Colosseum set dressing for the Proving Floor / Proving Grounds arena. Phase 0 art direction (owner): a ceremonial duelling platform ringed by spectators — standing stone where the map has walls, rough wooden cover where it has cover. Each role is a LIST of interchangeable variants; the board picks one per tile by a hash of the square, so a run is no longer the same mesh repeated. Walls are authored TALLER than a tile and VARIED in height (owner, session 25): a wall is a full line-of-sight blocker whatever its drawn height, so a taller, uneven colonnade reads more clearly as wall-not-cover and gives the arena presence — the renderer places a wall .glb at its own authored height (it does not scale walls), so height is a per-variant number here. Cover is authored at COVER_HEIGHT (0.45) and the renderer normalises it to crouch height on the tile's faced edge (COVER-EDGE); its VARIETY is the fence silhouette, since every cover variant ends up the same height. All cover is now thin WOODEN barricade — the wide masonry block was dropped (owner, session 25) because on a faced edge its full footprint swallowed the tile; a thin fence sits on the boundary and lets the board read through it. Colours are neutral stone and dark wood: MAP_PIPELINE §4 forbids a permanent fixture landing in a saturated UI colour family, and greys (r≈g≈b) and dark wood (every channel well under 130, luminance under 185) sit clear of the amber AoE and the team hues. ORIENTATION of cover is NOT set here: the map authors a per-tile `facing` (COVER-EDGE) and the renderer sits the barricade on that edge and turns it along the boundary. Walls have no facing and take a hashed quarter-turn per tile for variety.

variants.comment: The standing fluted column: square plinth, tapered fluted shaft, flared capital. Tall and slender.
A broken column: no capital, the shaft snapped short and uneven, fallen chunks at the base. The shortest of the three — a ruin — but still clearly taller than crouch cover.
A heavy column — the tallest, with a thick shaft, deeper flutes, and a broad plinth and capital. Weight and height next to the slender fluted one.
The rough wooden stake barricade: four uneven stakes lashed to a crossbar between two heavier posts. The lightest, thinnest fence.
A denser, taller-topped barricade — five stakes and a higher crossbar. A heavier stretch of the same fence line.
A rough three-stake palisade — fewer, chunkier timbers with big gaps and a low lashed rail. The gappiest of the three, so a run of cover does not read as one solid fence.
